description: HesabYar Phase 5-7 (۵خ — Workflows & automation): Procrastinate scheduler + maintenance jobs, rules engine v1 (when + conditions → closed safe actions, dry-run, audit), rules management UI, recurring invoices/journals (Jalali-aware), reminders (cheque/installment/cashbox/eNamad, SMS via the US-544 registry), and Xero-style bank auto-coding rules.

acceptanceCriteria: Procrastinate periodic jobs (from F1/US-501): reconciliation polling, Supply-wizard result read (execution runs on ir.cron INSIDE Tryton, not Procrastinate — HesabYar only reads the result), tranche.expected → due transition at maturity (the schedule belongs to P1/US-521; W1 only issues the transition), cheque/installment due alerts, inbox staleness alert

The ۵ج dunning sweep (currently on-demand via POST /dunning/run) runs on schedule; the US-544 SMS daily job runs on schedule; the store-sync endpoint (POST /integrations/{connector}/sync, US-533 deferred) runs on a 15-minute cadence
Jalali-aware scheduling: next_run computed in-app (no Jalali cron exists); Friday is the weekend default
Job registry: each job has an id, schedule, last run, next run, last outcome; failures go to the DLQ + review queue as inbox_dead_letter, never silent
REST endpoints to list jobs, trigger one run on demand, and enable/disable a job; scope jobs:manage (new scope if no fitting scope exists)
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Scheduler + maintenance jobs on Procrastinate: reconciliation polling, tranche transitions, due alerts, inbox staleness, dunning sweep, SMS job, store sync — all Jalali-aware.
userStories.notes: Wave A (first — the other stories build on the scheduler). Depends on US-501 (event platform + Procrastinate), US-521 (settlement tranches), US-541 (dunning), US-544 (SMS job), US-533 (store sync endpoint). The Supply wizard runs inside Tryton on ir.cron — HesabYar NEVER drives it from Procrastinate.
userStories.title: Scheduler + maintenance jobs (W1)

acceptanceCriteria: Rules engine v1: `when <event> + <conditions> → do <action>` — event from the 12 canonical event types (spec §10.2 + ADR 0004 + ADR 0005), conditions on event fields (amount ranges, channel, party, company), actions from a CLOSED SAFE SET ONLY: create draft / post via the policy gate / notify (in-app + email) / allocate (mapping)

Dry-run: a rule can be tested against past events (or a sample payload) showing exactly what it WOULD do, with no side effects; every dry-run and every live execution is audit-logged (rule id, event id, decision, outcome)
NO rule can auto-post without passing the 3-layer policy gate (F3) — a rule that would post is blocked by the gate exactly like a manual post; draft is the default
NO arbitrary user code execution (no 'Execute Python Code' action), no visual DAG builder, no BPMN/Temporal
REST endpoints for rules (CRUD, enable/disable, dry-run, execution history); scopes rules:read/rules:manage (new scopes if no fitting scope exists)
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Rules engine v1 core: event + conditions → closed safe actions, with dry-run and full audit; the policy gate is never bypassed.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-501 (events), US-503 (policy gate), US-552 (audit patterns). The closed action set is a SAFETY property — a test must prove an unknown action is rejected and a post action still goes through the gate.
userStories.title: Rules engine v1 core (W2)

acceptanceCriteria: Rules management UI (Persian RTL, VibeFarsi): list rules with status + last execution, create/edit form (event picker, condition builder, action picker from the closed set), enable/disable, dry-run panel showing the would-do result, execution history + audit log view
Rule ownership: user-defined rules are W3's — the UI makes clear which rules are user-defined vs system; B2 learned mappings enter the engine as SUGGESTIONS only, never as auto-rules
Every UI action calls the US-561 REST endpoints (no direct DB access from the frontend); tsc 0, eslint 0, vitest green, build green
Playwright: one rules journey (create → dry-run → enable → see an execution in history)
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Rules management UI: create/edit/enable/disable rules, dry-run panel, execution history and audit view.
userStories.notes: Wave C (needs US-561's API). Frontend house rules in apps/admin/AGENTS.md apply. B2 learned mappings (US-514/US-552) are suggestions, not rules — the UI must not present them as active automations.
userStories.title: Rules management UI (W2)

acceptanceCriteria: Recurring invoices + recurring journals: Jalali-aware schedules (monthly on a Jalali day, every N months, yearly on a Jalali date); each occurrence is created as a DRAFT by default (auto-post only with explicit opt-in, through the policy gate)
Preview: the next N occurrences with dates + amounts before saving; pause/resume; end date or occurrence count
Each generated document links to its recurring template + occurrence number; editing the template does not rewrite already-generated drafts
REST endpoints for templates (CRUD, preview, pause/resume, generated list); scopes invoices:write / journals:write as applicable
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Recurring invoices and journals with Jalali-aware schedules, draft by default, preview before saving.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-560 (scheduler — the recurring generator is a scheduled job), US-202 (journal drafts), US-204 (invoices). Jalali month lengths vary (Esfand 29/30 days) — a day-31 monthly recurrence must clamp honestly, never silently skip.
userStories.title: Recurring invoices + journals (W3)

acceptanceCriteria: Cheque due-soon reminders (3 days + 7 days before due), overdue-installment reminders, uncounted-cashbox reminders (cashbox not counted for more than N days, N user-configured), eNamad expiry reminders (expiry DISABLES gateway/BNPL service — §8.3 — so the reminder is a warning, not a suggestion)

SMS channel via the US-544 multi-provider registry (Kavenegar + sms.ir first built-ins; provider specifics user-entered, never hard-coded): due-installment + due-cheque reminders by SMS in addition to in-app + email; cost per SMS recorded; customer consent/opt-out honored; mobile numbers stored per the privacy policy
Reminder preferences per installation: which reminders are on, which channels (in-app/email/SMS), lead times; quiet hours honored
Reminders are idempotent (one reminder per event per lead-time, never duplicates); every sent reminder is logged with channel + cost
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Reminders: cheque due-soon, overdue installments, uncounted cashbox, eNamad expiry — in-app + email + SMS via the provider registry.
userStories.notes: Wave B. Depends on US-560 (scheduler), US-531/US-534 (cheque due dates), US-541 (overdue legs), US-516 (cashbox counts), US-544 (SMS registry + simulator — NO live SMS without credentials). eNamad expiry disabling gateway/BNPL service is a design rule (§8.3), not a suggestion.
userStories.title: Reminders incl. SMS channel (W3)

acceptanceCriteria: Xero-style bank rules for auto-coding statements: `when <statement-line pattern> (description contains / amount range / counterparty) → suggest <account + mapping>`; Suggest ← Auto promotion (a suggestion becomes automatic only after the user promotes it, threshold 3 confirmed suggestions — same pattern as US-552 mapping learning)
User-defined bank rules are W3 rules (managed in the US-562 UI); B2 learned mappings enter as suggestions only
Auto-coded lines still go through the policy gate + tie-out before posting; a wrong auto-code can be undone (the mapping is corrected, the journal is a draft until approved)

Playwright: workflows spec covering one rule journey (create → dry-run → live execution), one recurring template (create → preview), one bank rule (suggest → promote → auto-code); responsive checks at 360–390px
Targeted tests per story + affected-area tests written for CI; ruff + pyright clean
userStories.description: Xero-style bank auto-coding rules (Suggest → Auto) + the workflows Playwright spec.
userStories.notes: Wave C (last — needs US-561/US-562 + US-514 bank import). Depends on US-514 (statement import), US-552 (mapping learning pattern), US-561 (rules engine). The Suggest → Auto threshold (3) matches the US-552 mapping-learning threshold.
userStories.title: Bank auto-coding rules + workflows Playwright (W3)
